newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Van der Horst shares plunge on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Van der Horst shares plunge on rumours.

text.p: Shares in Singapore's Van der Horst took a bashing in late afternoon trade, falling to their lowest since 1993 on a slew of rumours, dealers and analysts said.
Among the rumours was that the engineering-based company would post disappointing results for its first half ended March 31, 1997.
At 0840 GMT, Van der Horst fell Singapore S$0.42, or 13.6 percent, to S$2.66 on heavy volume of 3.7 million shares.
The shares have not fallen so low since late 1993.
Its warrants also tumbled, by S$0.30 to S$1.74 on 36,000 units traded.
"The rumours are just circulating. I heard there are delays with their contracts and poor results," said one analyst who declined to be named.
"I expect the shares are going to be pressured to below S$2.00," said one dealer.
Since February, the Van der Horst share price has been under downward pressure, falling from a high of S$6.50 in February.
Dealers and analysts said they were expecting Van der Horst to release its first half results either on Friday or next week.
Officials at Van der Horst were not immediately available for comment.
